rationale: Code audit found survivor.py entry gates check regime CATEGORY (regime in ["range","reversal_watch"]) but never regime STABILITY, despite regime_engine.get_regime_stability() already existing and being unused. REGIME_CHANGE/HEDGE_EXIT_REGIME_CHANGE exits account for approx -22,139 of survivor total -31,362 loss over 20 days (~71%). Backfilled stability-at-entry (last 10 regime polls, same formula as engine): trades later exited via REGIME_CHANGE averaged 63.9 stability at entry (n~16 distinct, range 50-100); other exits averaged 70.8 (n~7 distinct, range 50-90). Signal is directionally supportive but noisy/overlapping -- not a confident cutoff by itself. Proposed 65.0 sits between the two group averages as a starting point for real gate-testing, not a data-derived optimum. All 4 sell trigger points (2 movement, 2 time-based) now gated behind this threshold, default 0.0 (off) so no behavior change until explicitly raised.
evidence: backfill_regime_stability.py (reconstructs get_regime_stability() against 17,417 logged regime polls, Jul 20 - Aug 17): REGIME_CHANGE-exit group avg=63.9 min=50.0 max=100.0 n=31 rows (~16 distinct entries, primary+hedge legs double-counted); other-exits avg=70.8 min=50.0 max=90.0 n=13 rows (~7 distinct). Code: strategy/survivor.py lines ~358,387 (movement triggers), ~1866 (shared time-based trigger gate). core/regime_engine.py:485 get_regime_stability(). Caveat: one entry (2026-08-13T10:58:51) has mismatched primary/hedge exit reasons (REGIME_CHANGE vs TP_HIT), indicating leg-level notes are an imperfect proxy for entry-level outcome.
